- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 70+ → 75+), especially if sentiment is positive; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion rule: average last 5–7 days + 10–15% buffer if sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underperforms in early days (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; use 3–5 day moving average or sentiment-weighted median for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is stable, model tends to drift downward; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days as baseline.
